name: A1-04 HTTP Request - safe retries and idempotency

meta.description: A retry is only safe if the second attempt cannot do the work twice. This shows the difference between an idempotency key derived from the business event and one generated per attempt - the second looks identical in the node and silently defeats the server's deduplication.
meta.author: Suyash Raj - https://rajsuyash.com/blog/n8n-error-handling-best-practices.html
meta.setup: None. httpbin.org/post echoes the headers it received, so you can read the key that actually went out.
meta.expectedOutput: Both POST nodes return 200. In 'Safe retry (stable key)' the echoed Idempotency-Key is the same on every attempt of the same order. In 'Unsafe retry (per-attempt key)' it changes on every execution, which is exactly what makes the retry unsafe.
meta.failureCases: Run the workflow twice. The stable key is identical across both runs for the same orderId - a correctly implemented server would reject the duplicate. The per-attempt key differs, so the server sees two distinct charges.

nodes.name: Safe retry (stable key)
nodes.notes: The key is derived from the order, so attempt 1, attempt 2 and a replay next Tuesday all send the same value. The server can recognise the repeat and return the original result instead of charging again.

nodes.name: Unsafe retry (per-attempt key)
nodes.notes: This is the common mistake. It has an idempotency header, it passes review, and it deduplicates nothing: every attempt announces itself as a new operation. The failure only shows up as duplicate charges after a timeout, which is the one moment nobody is reading logs.
